headings.text: Typical pattern: a one-shot "pick an item" workflow

blocks.html: MapEventDispatcher is ATAK's event bus for high-level map events (clicks, item added/removed, etc.). You get it from the MapView:
MapEventDispatcher dispatcher = getMapView().getMapEventDispatcher();

Subscribing

There are three subscription granularities:

// 1. ALL events, all items, all types
dispatcher.addMapEventListener(listener);

// 2. Only events of a specific type
dispatcher.addMapEventListener(MapEvent.ITEM_CLICK, listener);

// 3. Only events for one specific MapItem
dispatcher.addMapItemEventListener(mapItem, onMapEventListener);

Each has a matching removeMapEventListener(...). Always unregister in your MapComponent teardown (onDestroyImpl) so listeners don't outlive the plugin.

The listener stack (suppressing other handlers)

MapEventDispatcher manages its listeners as a stack, and only the listeners on top of the stack receive events. This is how a tool can temporarily take over an event (e.g. "the next map-item click belongs to me") without other handlers also reacting:

dispatcher.pushListeners();   // copy current listeners onto a new top-of-stack
// clear/replace listeners so only yours are active, then handle your one event...
// when done:
dispatcher.popListeners();    // discard your temporary set, restore the prior state

• **pushListeners()** copies the current top set and pushes the copy — your changes apply only to that copy.
  • **popListeners()** discards the top set and restores the subscription state from before the matching push.

Typical pattern: a one-shot "pick an item" workflow

A widget that needs the user to click one item, then go back to normal:

  1. On activate: pushListeners(), then register a single item-click listener (and optionally clear others) so nothing else reacts.
  2. On the click: handle it, then popListeners() to restore normal map behaviour.

This keeps your transient interaction from firing every other map handler in the app.
